title: Relative pronoun: agreement and function
subtitle: Its form agrees with its antecedent; its case belongs to its own clause.
overview: A relative pronoun agrees with its antecedent in gender and number, but its case comes from its job inside the relative clause.
This single distinction prevents many incorrect translations.

sections.title: Agreement versus clause function
rows: the word which you hear — ὃν is object
the word which remains — ὃς is subject
